newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee turns lower on hedge sales by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee turns lower on hedge sales by close.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures took a downward turn by the finish on Friday on light hedge selling but conditions were extremely dull.
The day's volume was a paltry 2,158 lots, again dominated by May/July and July/Sept switches as players rolled their positions further forward.

May, which held steady for most of the day, slipped into the minus column in the late afternoon as hedge sellers emerged. By the close, the front-position contract was $15 down at $1,565 a tonne after a high of $1,595.
The contract had been trapped in a series of relatively tight ranges this week, finding it difficult to hold above $1,600.
"It's wandering sideways...but there is no actual dynamic which would say there is a lot of support there," said Susan Rigg, a technical analyst at Chart Analysis.
"You can't really say it's doing anything other than consolidating its good rise so far," she said.
On the charts, May is seen supported at $1,545, then $1,535, while resistance is pegged at between $1,610 and $1,620.
The second-month July contract finished $15 easier at $1,570. May/July switches were earlier seen traded at between $10 and $15.
The futures market has virtually come to a standstill, hovering in a tight $1,545-$1,600 range all week on a lack of interest from either side of the market.
Origin sellers have stepped back, awaiting for more lucrative values, while roaster stocks have risen to more comfortable levels.
Coffee consumption usually drops during the Western hemisphere summer.
"This is not the high roasting season for coffee," said one trader. "Roasters are buying to meet their minimal requirements, they are not buying additional volumes."
Furthermore, the higher retail prices across Europe following the recent market rally could also dampen consumption.
The market kept a close watch on Colombia, where truck drivers have threatened to down their tools on April 20.
Traders said the coffee export sector could be crippled if the strike, if materialised, lasts more than ten days.

A series of data are due later on Friday and early next week. They include the U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders report, scheduled at the close of U.S. trading on Friday, and the U.S. March green coffee stocks on Tuesday.
LIFFE's March certified stocks data are also due to be released on Tuesday. Traders expected little change in the CFTC report.
